articles.title: Bet365 presenta su nuevo posicionamiento de marca a nivel mundial, 'Sabemos de apuestas', con el lanzamiento de la campaña 'Razones'

articles.summary: La compañía bet365 ha marcado el regreso de la temporada de fútbol con un nuevo posicionamiento que se ha materializado a través de 'Razones', su campaña de marketing de apoyo
articles.body: El concepto 'Sabemos de apuestas' salió a la luz esta semana, evolucionando desde la marca anterior de la empresa, 'Marcamos la diferencia', y sirve para celebrar los más de 25 años de bet365 al frente de las apuestas digitales. Esta nueva campaña fue desarrollada tras una extensa investigación con clientes y equipos de toda la compañía, y expresa lo que desde hace mucho tiempo constituye la esencia de bet365: décadas de experiencia construida a través del aprendizaje continuo, la innovación y el perfeccionamiento de la experiencia en las apuestas. Con 'Sabemos de apuestas', la empresa no busca afirmar simplemente que son expertos, sino que cuenta la historia de cómo ponen su experiencia en práctica para el beneficio de sus clientes, garantizando que éstos disfruten de una experiencia mejor, más sencilla y más satisfactoria. Desde la plataforma aseguran que la historia está lejos de terminarse, ya que la compañía se encuentra siempre aprendiendo y mejorando. De este modo, a medida que bet365 y el sector de las apuestas sigan creciendo y evolucionando, también lo hará la experiencia que ofrecen a los usuarios. Creada en colaboración con Drummond Central, el asociado estratégico y creativo de bet365, la campaña publicitaria 'Razones' se lanzó primeramente en el Reino Unido y Dinamarca, siendo Alemania y España los siguientes países en incorporarla poco después. Se trata de una campaña integral que abarca canales propios, programas, audios, prensa, patrocinios y publicidad exterior. El anuncio publicitario fue dirigido por Jack Driscoll de Academy, producido por Tom Cartwright y grabado en Praga en colaboración con la empresa de servicios Unit Sofa. La narrativa de la campaña comienza reflexionando sobre las décadas que la marca ha dedicado a perfeccionar la experiencia de apuestas, para luego pasar a los momentos centrados en el cliente, los cuales están respaldados por una serie de "Razones" enumeradas. Esta enumeración abierta tiene como objetivo reflejar la magnitud de la experiencia y los beneficios que la compañía ha construido a lo largo de más de dos décadas y que continúan en constante crecimiento. Alex Sefton, director de marketing global de bet365, declaró que en la empresa nunca se han caracterizado por quedarse quietos, y que 'Sabemos de apuestas' refleja los 25 años que han pasado perfeccionando lo que hacen y cómo usan ese conocimiento para crear la mejor experiencia posible para sus usuarios. Además, señaló que 'Razones' es la primera expresión de este nuevo concepto, proporcionándoles una plataforma clara y segura para demostrar, en lugar de solo contar, por qué su experiencia importa, abriendo así un nuevo e interesante capítulo para la marca. Por su parte, el director creativo de Drummond Central, Kevin Lynn, explicó que 'Sabemos de apuestas' muestra a bet365 en su faceta más segura, mientras que 'Razones' pone el foco en la propia marca para preguntar qué hay detrás de dicha experiencia. Lynn detalló que el objetivo era que la experiencia de la empresa fuera tangible en lugar de abstracta, por lo que cada razón tiene su momento específico en pantalla, conformando un tipo diferente de narración que está sólidamente respaldada por los 25 años de trayectoria de la compañía. El reposicionamiento de la marca no termina con esta campaña, ya que el nuevo concepto cobrará vida en cada punto de contacto de bet365. Esto incluye, entre otros, sus canales digitales, la aplicación móvil, sus plataformas de redes sociales, patrocinios, asociaciones, la comunicación directa con el cliente y la televisión. Adicionalmente, bet365 ha destacado su orgullo por incorporar plenamente el juego responsable en esta nueva plataforma creativa. La compañía continuará impulsando su campaña "JUEGO SEGURO | bet365", asegurando que el mensaje de juego responsable sea una pieza central de todo el marketing publicitario de 'Razones'. En este sentido, la empresa reitera su compromiso con un juego más seguro, promoviendo las apuestas exclusivamente como una actividad de ocio para mayores de 18 años que debe realizarse siempre con control y responsabilidad.

articles.title: NHL training camp faces early uncertainty with Connor Hellebuyck and Winnipeg Jets situation unresolved
articles.summary: NHL News: As the Winnipeg Jets gear up for NHL training camp, questions arise about goalie Connor Hellebuyck, who may not report due to his trade request. Will the team find a suitable deal?
articles.body: The Winnipeg Jets are getting ready for NHL training camp amid heavy speculation about Connor Hellebuyck. NHL insider Darren Dreger reports the star goaltender is not expected to report when Winnipeg’s camp opens on Thursday, September 17.It comes after Hellebuyck publicly asked to be traded and a summer of uncertainty about his future with the Winnipeg Jets. The organization has looked at potential trade scenarios, but there’s been no deal reported that matches the type of return general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff is seeking.Connor Hellebuyck absence creates questions for Winnipeg Jets training campConnor Hellebuyck unlikely to show up to Winnipeg Jets training camp, but that could change. The report adds urgency to a trade situation that has gone unresolved all off-season.Hellebuyck publicly asked for a trade after the Winnipeg Jets missed the playoffs in 2025-26. The netminder has five years left on the seven-year contract he signed with Winnipeg, which has an average annual value of $8.5 million. He also has a complete no-movement clause.The Winnipeg Jets are in a bind as they consider Hellebuyck’s trade request and the need to stay competitive in the Central Division. There’s been interest in the league, including previous talks with the Buffalo Sabres, but the trade market has yet to produce a package that has convinced Winnipeg to part with its franchise goaltender, reports have said.That's a rough spot to be in going into camp. Winnipeg has already added goaltender Stuart Skinner, giving themselves an important layer of insurance if Hellebuyck is moved down the line. Still, that would be a big change to the roster, to replace a three-time Vezina Trophy winner.How Connor Hellebuyck situation affects WinnipegUncertainty ahead for the Winnipeg Jets after a difficult 2025-26 campaign. The club finishedatop the NHL standings in 2025-26, but then missed the playoffs, raising questions about the direction of the roster heading into the new campaign.The team was preparing as if Hellebuyck would be with the team in Winnipeg, captain Adam Lowry said. Defenseman Josh Morrissey recently said the trade request affected him on a personal level. Mark Scheifele also chimed in on the situation, emphasising the necessity for players to stay focused on the team.The next big development could come when training camp officially opens; how Hellebuyck lands whether he reports, stays away from the team or is moved via trade will go a long way toward defining Winnipeg’s immediate goaltending plans and could become one of the NHL’s most closely watched stories before the regular season kicks off.Connor Hellebuyck probably won’t show up for Winnipeg Jets’ training camp, adding uncertainty to team goaltending plans. The star netminder has asked for a trade, but Winnipeg hasn’t been able to find a deal. articles.title: Nebraska, Notre Dame Announce Future Home-And-Home Football Series
articles.summary: Nebraska and Notre Dame announced a home-and-home football series that will take place in 2032 and 2033.
articles.body: Keep your schedule open in the fall of 2032 and 2033. That's because the Nebraska Cornhuskers and Notre Dame Fighting Irish announced on Wednesday morning that the two schools will take part in a college football home-and-home series in 2032 and 2033. The Fighting Irish will travel to Lincoln to play Nebraska on Oct. 30, 2032, and the Cornhuskers will travel to South Bend to play Notre Dame on Oct. 29, 2033. "The series with Notre Dame is the type of matchup that college football fans circle on their calendars years in advance," Nebraska Director of Athletics Troy Dannen said in a statement. "Our fans have a tremendous appreciation for the history of college football and iconic venues. We are excited to welcome Notre Dame and their fans to Lincoln in 2032, and I know our fans will travel to South Bend in full force in 2033." The scheduled 2032 game will be the first time the two programs square off since the Cornhuskers beat the Fighting Irish in Nebraska on Sept. 8, 2001, 27-10, and just the third time since 1948. Nebraska is 8-7-1 all time against Notre Dame. As for the present, both teams are 2-0 in the 2026 college football season, with the Cornhuskers getting home victories over the Ohio Bobcats (49-21) and Bowling Green Falcons (56-7) and the No. 3 AP-ranked Fighting Irish defeating the Wisconsin Badgers at Lambeau Field (41-13) and the Rice Owls at home (52-0). Nebraska's Big Ten season opener comes on the road against the Michigan State Spartans on Sept. 26, and it has four AP Top 25-ranked teams on its remaining schedule (Indiana, Oregon, Ohio State and Iowa). Meanwhile, Notre Dame has three AP Top-25 ranked teams on its remaining schedule: BYU, Miami and SMU. Both Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule and Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman signed new contracts with their respective schools within the last year. The Cornhuskers are a combined 21-19 under Rhule since 2023, while the Fighting Irish are a combined 45-12 under Freeman since he took over as head coach during the 2021 season, highlighted by reaching the 2024 College Football Playoff National Championship.

articles.title: Verstappen takes 35 minutes to complete epic kart challenge
articles.summary: Max Verstappen delivered another remarkable demonstration of his racecraft by winning the inaugural Max vs 100 karting challenge at Silverstone. Starting 101...
articles.body:
Max Verstappen delivered another remarkable demonstration of his racecraft by winning the inaugural Max vs 100 karting challenge at Silverstone. Starting 101st and last on a grid filled with 100 opponents, the four-time Formula 1 world champion completed his charge to first place in just 35 minutes, well before the planned 30-lap distance had been completed.

The event placed Verstappen in identical karting machinery to a field featuring athletes, content creators, personalities and motorsport figures. The objective was straightforward but daunting: pass every one of the 100 drivers ahead of him. Any competitor overtaken by Verstappen was eliminated from the race.

The scale of the challenge made it unlike a typical kart race. Verstappen was required to thread through a massive field on a purpose-built Silverstone layout, where traffic, congestion and potential contact were as significant as outright pace. Before the event, he had acknowledged that overtaking 100 people would be difficult and predicted "carnage" among the karts ahead.

That prediction proved accurate almost immediately. At the start, the field became compressed through the early corners and a bottleneck developed at a hairpin. Verstappen used the disorder to make exceptional progress.

He overtook 64 karts on the opening lap, moving from 101st to 37th despite a yellow-flag interruption and a brief trip onto the grass.

His advance continued at an extraordinary pace. By lap two, he had climbed to 36th. By lap three, he was 26th and within striking distance of the leaders.

Verstappen reached the top 20 on lap four, the top 10 by lap six, and fifth position by lap seven. The expected 30-lap challenge was rapidly turning into a short, decisive pursuit.

There was one minor setback when Verstappen ran off track on lap six and lost a Go-Pro from his kart. However, the incident did little to halt his momentum. Once he found clean air, he continued to reduce the gap to the front runners with relentless speed.

The format included a tactical "fast lap" shortcut. Verstappen's rivals could use theirs during the opening half of the race, while Verstappen's own opportunity was reserved for the second half. Organisers even gave the leaders additional fast-lap opportunities in an apparent attempt to keep the contest alive. It was not enough.

By lap nine, Verstappen had moved into fourth and was closing rapidly on the leading trio: Dutch journalist Jacky Martens, YouTuber Zac Alsop and Red Bull Powertrains employee Lewis Osler. Osler briefly delayed Verstappen with strong defensive driving and an extra fast lap, but the Formula 1 champion soon erased the advantage.

On lap 15, Verstappen completed the comeback. He passed Martens and Alsop to secure victory, completing the journey from 101st to first after approximately half the scheduled race distance.

Verstappen said: "My first lap was quite incredible," he said. "There was a lot happening and actually a few cars got stuck and I always managed to be on the other side, so didn't get stuck.

"And that made me get like 60 people in the first lap. So that just helps a lot, getting through to the front."

He's asked where it ranks in his victories. "I think this is the best one yet!"

The result highlighted the karting instincts that underpinned Verstappen's rise to Formula 1.

articles.title: See Where Boston College, Boston University and More Rank in Preseason Hockey East Poll
articles.summary: As college hockey nears, the first Hockey East poll is out.
articles.body:
College hockey begins in nearly two weeks, and the preseason Hockey East poll indicates multiple Boston schools could be at the center of the national conversation once again.

While Providence leads the way, receiving eight of 11 first-place votes, Boston University received two first-place votes and Boston College wasn't far behind.

Both the Terriers and the Eagles, who have each played for a national championship in the last three years but came up short, are hoping to find their way to Washington D.C. for the Frozen Four in April.

Here's a look at the preseason Hockey East poll and where Boston schools rank.

Providence came in comfortably at No. 1, receiving the bulk of first-place votes, while UMass slotted in second despite receiving fewer first-place votes than Boston University.

The Friars won the Hockey East regular season title in the spring, though eighth-seeded Merrimack made a surprising run to win the conference tournament and secure a trip to the NCAA Tournament. No Boston school reached the NCAA Tournament, as the Hockey East only sent Providence, UConn and Merrimack; all three lost in the first round.

Boston College slots in fourth out of 11 teams in the preseason Hockey East poll, the highest-ranked team without a first-place vote. The Eagles finished fourth in the conference last season.

Boston University ranks third in the preseason Hockey East poll, with two first-place votes. The Terriers finished a disappointing sixth in the conference last season, missing the NCAA Tournament after three consecutive trips to the Frozen Four.

Northeastern ranks eighth in the preseason Hockey East poll, ahead of only New Hampshire, UMass Lowell and Vermont. The Huskies finished seventh in the conference last season and last reached the NCAA Tournament in 2022.

articles.title: Cody Rhodes’ Wild Idea For Angle Involving The Rock’s Daughter That Never Happened
articles.summary: Cody Rhodes has revealed there was once a very different plan for his soul storyline with The Rock, one that […]
articles.body:
Cody Rhodes has revealed there was once a very different plan for his soul storyline with The Rock , one that would have involved his daughter, Ava, instead of Dwayne Johnson himself.

Speaking on his podcast, " What Do You Wanna Talk About?" , Rhodes explained that when The Rock demanded his soul during their 2025 on-screen rivalry, he briefly considered redirecting the entire angle toward Ava, who was serving as NXT General Manager at the time.

"When the Final Boss asked me for my soul, I thought, what would've been funny, is to relent and give my soul, but not to him. This is at a time when you were the NXT General Manager, to you. I thought, 'That's got legs. I'll never say a word again. She'll speak,'" Rhodes said.

Ava responded to the pitch with immediate enthusiasm, agreeing the concept had real potential if it had made it to television that year.

"I think we would've crushed that," she said.

Rhodes echoed the sentiment, noting he has no reservations about playing a villain if the story calls for it.

"We would've crushed that. People are often like, 'You don't want to be a bad guy.' I'm open to all things. Whatever is the best. I thought that would've been a real good spin," Rhodes said.

"I would've loved to have done that," Ava added.

The conversation turned to how Johnson himself would have reacted to being cut out of the payoff after driving the 2025 storyline forward. Rhodes asked Ava directly, and she said she believed he would have supported the swap.

"I think he would've been all for it. Absolutely," Ava said.

Rhodes admitted he was surprised the idea had never come up between Ava and Johnson.

"I can't believe you never told him," Rhodes said.

Ava explained the timing never lined up for that conversation, since she had no advance knowledge of Johnson's involvement before it aired.

"I don't think it ever came up because I think he was beating you up, asking you for your soul. I don't think I knew he was coming back that day. I had no context of what the promo would be. I just saw it and was like, 'Soul is crazy,'" Ava said.

Rhodes closed out the discussion by suggesting the concept isn't necessarily dead, even though the moment for it has technically passed.

"I think we might have had something. Who knows, we might still have something. I thought it was such a fun spin. My soul goes to you and we would've wreaked havoc. Sold out every night. That was our idea. It never happened," Rhodes said.

Ava left the door open for a future version of the storyline.

"Who knows, maybe it could still happen. Never say never," she said.

Opinion: This Idea Would Have Wrecked The Real 2025 Plan

As fun as the pitch sounds in hindsight, redirecting the soul angle to Ava would have almost certainly derailed the actual plan WWE was building toward in 2025: John Cena's heel turn. The entire point of The Rock inserting himself into the Cody Rhodes story was to set up Cena's alliance with him and the heel run that followed, culminating in Cena taking the title off Rhodes at WrestleMania 41 with Rock's help. That storyline only works if The Rock is positioned as the direct threat holding something over Rhodes. Handing the soul off to Ava instead removes Rock from the center of the conflict at the exact moment WWE needed him there to justify Cena's turn.

There's also a practical problem with the pitch that Rhodes and Ava didn't address: Ava was NXT General Manager, not a main roster act, and pulling her into a top-of-the-card story with Rhodes and Johnson would have meant either promoting her creative role dramatically overnight or awkwardly writing around her NXT duties. Neither option serves the Cena payoff, and both would have added complications to a storyline that was already carrying a lot of moving pieces heading into WrestleMania season.

None of this means the idea was bad in a vacuum. It's a clever swerve, and it clearly would have given Ava a bigger spotlight than she got in 2025. But WWE picked the version of the story that led to Cena's heel turn for a reason, and that version needed Johnson, not Ava, standing across from Rhodes.

articles.title: NFL Insider: Cleveland Browns Have ‘Horrendous Vibes All Around’
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns weren’t very competitive last season, but general manager Andrew Berry has been building this roster up for […]
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns weren't very competitive last season, but general manager Andrew Berry has been building this roster up for a few years now. The hope is that first-year head coach Todd Monken can spark a change that leads to more wins after Kevin Stefanski mustered just five in 2025.

Yet, after losing 34-10, it's clear that Week 1 wasn't the start that the Browns were looking for. Starting quarterback Deshaun Watson didn't perform any better in Monken's offense than he did under coach Stefanski, and after moving on from Jim Schwartz, the defense looks even worse. Now, as one NFL insider says, the vibes in Cleveland are "horrendous."

No one really expected the Browns to beat a Jaguars team that won 13 games a season ago in Week 1. Still, after revamping the offense, there was hope that a new coach could lead an inspired effort, much like the ones witnessed in Arizona , Baltimore , and New York. Yet, that's not what happened in Cleveland.

Now, as ESPN's Dan Graziano suggests, the Browns "aren't going anywhere with Watson," and he doesn't think things will improve in Cleveland until the organization admits that.

"It's hard for me to be surprised when someone who insists on starting Watson at quarterback in 2026 doesn't have success. There are some things to like about Cleveland's roster, and I believe Monken knows how to coach, but the Browns aren't going anywhere with Watson. Until they admit that and make a change, I don't see how things can improve. Just horrendous vibes all the way around."

It's hard to envision how things get much better from here. But then again, it was just one game. Now Watson and the Browns have a chance to head back to the drawing board after breaking down the film. In an ideal world, they'll identify ways they can improve and make the necessary changes. If not, it's only a matter of time before Shedeur Sanders gets another opportunity to be the starter.

articles.title: Browns blasted for 'horrendous vibes' thanks to Deshaun Watson QB decision
articles.summary: This ESPN analyst didn't hold back in his criticism of the Browns.
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson was named the starting quarterback for Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars , and predictably, it went horribly wrong. They lost 34-10, which could've been 34-3 if it weren't for a last-minute garbage-time touchdown.

After the brutal loss, Todd Monken stuck by Watson as the starter, backing him as QB1 for Week 2 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . But plenty of fans, and even media members, are over Watson being the Browns ' QB.

ESPN's Dan Graziano blasted the Browns for their "horrendous vibes" with Watson as the starter. He called out Todd Monken for the decision with Watson and has a hard time believing things will improve so long as Watson is the starter.

Browns blasted for Deshaun Watson decision by ESPN analyst

"It's hard for me to be surprised when someone who insists on starting Watson at quarterback in 2026 doesn't have success," Graziano writes of Monken. "There are some things to like about Cleveland 's roster, and I believe Monken knows how to coach, but the Browns aren't going anywhere with Watson."

Graziano continued, "Until they admit that and make a change, I don't see how things can improve. Just horrendous vibes all the way around."

This is some brutal analysis for the Browns and Watson, but it's an especially bad indictment of Monken.

The Browns head coach has stuck by Watson as the starter, despite Watson clearly being one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL in a starting job.

Cleveland would do well to move on from Watson sooner rather than later, and taking him out of the starting job is Monken's duty.

But he's sending Watson back out there in Week 2 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and Graziano has little interest in the Browns while Monken keeps making this decision.

It's hard not to see the Browns' vibes as "horrendous," as Graziano noted, as Watson being the starter provides no upside, and the beef between him and the Browns fanbase certainly doesn't help his case.

Graziano put the Browns and Monken on blast for continuing to start Watson, and while it's harsh, it's a fairly accurate analysis of the Browns' current status and outlook.

Until they make a switch, whether it's to Shedeur Sanders , Dillon Gabriel , or even Taylen Green , the vibes with this Browns team are going to be, as Graziano put it, horrendous.

articles.title: Tempo news: Marina Mabrey’s season-ending injury update comes with silver lining
articles.summary: The Toronto Tempo have four games remaining in the regular season, but they’re going to have to play those games with All-Star guard Marina Mabrey who has be...
articles.body:
The Toronto Tempo have four games remaining in the regular season, but they're going to have to play those games with All-Star guard Marina Mabrey who has been dealing with injury issues. The Tempo have already been eliminated from playoff contention , but they can still play spoiler as two of their remaining games are against teams still battling for playoff positioning.

The good news for the Tempo, however, regarding Marina Mabrey 's injury is that she will not need surgery , as per Annie Costabile of The Athletic. articles.title: 7 marathons in 7 days? Tampa couple is running around the world
articles.summary: Jill and Dougin Walker have big plans for the new year. The Tampa couple will compete together in the World Marathon Challenge, running seven marathons on se...
articles.body:
Jill and Dougin Walker have big plans for the new year.

The Tampa couple will compete together in the World Marathon Challenge, running seven marathons on seven continents in seven consecutive days with more than 60 competitors.

"I don't really see us training for this," said Jill, 59. "The amount of Ironmans we do pretty much every weekend, our bodies are like 'Let's go, what are we doing this weekend?'"

The 2027 World Marathon Challenge begins Jan. 30 with a marathon in Antarctica.

From there, competitors travel around the globe to run in Cape Town, South Africa; Perth, Australia; Dubai, United Arab Emirates; Madrid, Spain; and Fortaleza, Brazil before finishing with their seventh marathon in Miami on Feb. 5.

Jill and Dougin Walker will each run 183.4 miles while completing all seven marathons within 168 hours.

The husband-and-wife endurance athletes are no strangers to travel.

The Walkers are part of a five-person club whose members have completed every Ironman triathlon in the world.

They once competed in an Ironman challenge in Vietnam, and the following weekend they were in Jacksonville for another one.

In 2023, the couple completed six Ironman races on six continents in just six weeks.

The World Marathon will bring them to Antarctica for the first time.

Dougin, 61, said the travel for the World Marathon will be interesting, but they'll adjust with some ease because of how much they already travel.

"Jill's really good at sleeping anywhere, so she's fine," Dougin said. "I'll probably have more of a sleep-issue hangover by the end of the trip."

For the Walkers, taking on endurance challenges together has become something of a way of life.

Their wedding was during an Ironman in Cozumel.

They stopped after the first loop of the bike course, got married in a 30-minute ceremony and then returned to the course to finish the race.

"We just fit perfectly," Jill said. "We both go to bed at the same time because we want to go to bed at the same time, not because the other one is. We both wake up super early. We both love any kind of adventure."

A marathon experience like this is also a social event. "I'm looking forward to meeting everyone, making new friends, and we have a couple of other friends that will also be doing it," Jill said. "That'll be fun, too, to be doing it with them."

What's next for the Walkers after the World Marathon? More endurance challenges lie ahead.

They will travel to South Africa for the 100th Comrades Marathon in June 2027.

"It's the big event in the running world," Dougin said. "We thought it'd be really cool to be there for that. It's one I wanted to do for a while."

Both are longtime Boston Marathon runners; Jill is planning to complete her 15th consecutive Boston Marathon next year, and this will be Dougin's 12th.

articles.title: JR Ritchie is back and he is making the start against the Cubs
articles.summary: The Braves look for win number 90 on the season behind the return of JR Ritchie
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves are inching closer to clinching the division with their magic number at five with their win last night against the Chicago Cubs .

It appears that the Braves will not catch the Dodgers for the second seed and first round bye, which is likely why the decision was made to bring up JR Ritchie to pitch this evening in the spot where Chris Sale was originally supposed to start to keep him rested. The last thing the Braves need right now is a fatigued or injured Chris Sale.

Ritchie has appeared in fourteen games so far this season to include eight starts. He pitched 58.0 innings of 4.50 ERA ball. This led to him getting sent back down in early August, but he has been fantastic in AAA as of late. Two starts ago for the Stripers he went 6.2 innings and amassed fifteen strikeouts to one walk. In his last start he went 6.0 innings where he struck out nine to one walk. He still struggles with the long ball, giving up three in his last two starts.

Of the eight starts at the MLB level Ritchie made this year, one of them was against the Cubs way back in May. It was arguably one of his best starts. He only went 4.1 innings, but he held the Cubs to two hits and one earned run, but he walked three.

It will be interesting to see how many innings he goes this evening because outside of his seven-inning debut, he never pitched more than 5.1 innings with three of his starts not even reaching 5.0. However, in the minors he has been working on longer starts pitching between 5.1 to 6.2 in his last four starts for the Stripers.

Since the Cubs have only faced Ritchie once in a short start, no player has more than two at-bats against him. The two players who were able to get a hit off him were Alex Bregman and Carson Kelly .

Shota Imanaga will be taking the mound for the Cubs and he is having a solid year. It has not been as great as his rookie campaign but is right on par with his performance last season in terms of ERA+ and FIP. He has pitched 162.1 innings and is on pace to pas his career high of 173.1 if he gets two more starts in. He holds an ERA of 3.88 and a WHIP of 1.121.

Imanaga had a rough first half in terms of ERA. Through his first thirteen starts his ERA was up to 4.74. Since then, he has settled down and carries an ERA of 3.13 over sixteen starts. He did pitch against the Braves and JR Ritchie in May where he gave up two earned runs on five hits over 7.0 innings. The Braves won that game 4-1.

Ozzie Albies leads the Braves in at-bats against Imanaga with twelve, and it is no surprise that he has been successful with a 1.334 OPS since Imanaga is a LHP. Matt Olson has eleven at-bats against Imanaga and carries a .455 average and 1.136 OPS in that span. Drake Baldwin has also been successful in six at-bats holding a 1.333 OPS to include a HR. The rest of the team has either not faced Imanaga before or has struggled.

Last night the Braves exposed that the Cubs' bullpen has been one of the luckiest in MLB this season if we look at their ERA against their expected ERA (xERA). Their season xERA is in the bottom four in MLB, while their actual ERA is in the best twelve.

If the Braves can get to the bullpen early, that is where they can do the most damage. It seems that all season long, the bullpen is there the Braves make most of their offense happen in general, but against the Cubs, it is especially true.

articles.title: Bill Simmons suggests dramatic change the LA Clippers need to make after Kawhi Leonard controversy
articles.summary: Bill Simmons has encouraged the Los Angeles Clippers to make some drastic changes after the recent salary cap circumvention scandal involving Kawhi Leonard’s...
articles.body:
Bill Simmons has encouraged the Los Angeles Clippers to make some drastic changes after the recent salary cap circumvention scandal involving Kawhi Leonard 's 2021 contract extension.

The Clippers have not only forfeited five first-round picks, but owner Steve Ballmer has been fined $30 million and received a year-long suspension, as have executives Gillian Zucker and Lawrence Frank (six months).

Leonard has since been traded to the Toronto Raptors for Brandon Ingram , Gradey Dick and two first-round picks. Although this appears a positive start to the Clippers' rebuild, Simmons believes they are beyond repair.

Bill Simmons' dramatic proposal for the Los Angeles Clippers

Bill Simmons has shared the controversial view that the Los Angeles Clippers should do more than simply rebuild. As LA's second NBA team and a franchise that has consistently struggled to meet expectations, the Clippers could be a prime candidate for a rebrand.

Simmons also highlighted that the Clippers have never made the Finals or even retired a jersey number. Who knows whether a rebrand would help them on the court, but at this stage, it is worth trying almost anything.

Simmons said, "Should they just change their name? Is this it? Is it rebrand time? And have we had a rebrand over the years in the NBA that has actually worked? And the answer to that is: maybe not. We had the Brooklyn Nets , the New Orleans Pelicans , and a Charlotte rebrand with the expansion team. Do rebrands work? Can it work with a sports franchise?

"And would you call it LA? I always thought they should be called the Hollywood Knights, even though they're not in Hollywood. Or you could call it Hollywood Nights with an 'N'. Either way, it would just feel completely different.

"I think they need to do something like that now. Granted, everybody who would be involved in that decision is suspended for a year. So I don't even know if they can do it. But I just wonder, have we run the course?

"Has 50 years of the Clippers just being a train wreck and coming up with scandals that we didn't even know could exist. Is it just time to start over? They don't even have a retired number. They've never made the finals. Can you just reset this right now in some way?"

Clippers fans will probably not be pleased with Simmons' suggestion to turn the franchise upside down following their recent struggles. The team has already faced significant consequences from the salary cap scandal and will not want another setback.

articles.title: The Cubs won’t get to 3 million tickets sold this year
articles.summary: The Cubs will fall a bit short of the milestone.
articles.body:
In 2025, the Cubs crossed the three million tickets sold line for the first time since 2019, and wound up with a paid attendance of 3,017,983, or 37,259 per date.

That included two "home" games at the Tokyo Dome which had paid attendance of 42,365 and 42,367, above Wrigley Field's current capacity of 41,649. For the 79 dates at Wrigley Field in 2025, the Cubs sold 2,933,251 tickets, or 37,129 per date.

They won't get to the three million mark this year, as with four dates remaining the paid attendance figure stands at 2,828,000, which is 172,000 short of that milestone. The Cubs would have to have paid attendance of 43,000 or more for the last four dates, which isn't going to happen. They'll probably wind up around 30,000 or so short of three million, so the average Wrigley crowd, which is currently 36,727, will also come up a little short of last year. The 2026 figures to date rank sixth in MLB in both total and average, behind the Dodgers , Yankees, Padres, Blue Jays and Phillies .

The team's performance is going to wind up about the same this year compared to last, so what are the factors driving this small decrease?

In my view, it's got to be the weather, which has been pretty awful all summer in Chicago — cooler than usual early in the season, then rainy for the last several weeks.

In 2025, the Cubs had 22 paid crowds at Wrigley of 40,000 or more, including two that crossed the 41,000 mark. This year there have been just 12 paid crowds of 40,000 or more at Wrigley Field, and the largest was 40,706, June 20 against the Blue Jays. (I think it's pretty safe to say that none of the remaining four dates will have a paid attendance of 40,000 or more.)

Additionally, the Cubs had five weekdays in March and April this year with crowds of under 30,000. Last year they had four such dates — and if the schedule is played out as listed in 2027 (NARRATOR: "It probably won't."), there will again be five of those.

Of course, we all hope there will be more than just four dates remaining at Wrigley Field this year, and that the Cubs will at the very least host a Wild Card series at the end of September/beginning of October.

articles.title: FSU standing out to 2028 defensive lineman
articles.summary: The Florida State Seminoles are making big waves in the recruiting of 2028 defensive lineman Fine Taufatofua Vailahi.
articles.body:
Florida State has two commitments in their 2028 recruiting class, and they're looking for more. Defensive lineman Fine Taufatofua Vailahi, who transfered from Byron Nelson High School in Texas to West High School in Utah, is a recruit they have their eyes on.

His recruitment has picked up tremendously throughout the spring and summer. As he evaluates things, FSU is one of the programs that standout to him.

"There are a lot of coaches and programs show me a lot of love. And some new ones have been coming in, too. I would say Florida State , Tennessee , UCLA , Kansas State , Oklahoma , Houston, a few others are in there for sure," Vailahi told 247Sports .

Vailahi got an offer from Florida State back in January after he attended one of their Junior Day events. The 6-foot-2, 255-pounder spoke on his experience in Tallahassee.

"Florida State, when I went down there in the past, it was great," said Vailahi. "The coaches there were all high energy guys, and Mike Norvell has some serious energy in him. When I saw him moving around, the energy he carries himself with, I was thinking it might be a move."

FSU has also made Vailahi feel like a priority with their approach.

"That all shows in the energy they brought to recruiting me," Vailahi said. "And they welcomed me as if I'm already one of their players. The love they showed me, sending me stuff about the program and videos about the program, it's showing the love they have for me. And stuff like that, that's what I really care about."

The next step for Florida State is to get Vailahi on campus for a game visit this season if possible.

articles.title: ESPN app streaming guide: How to watch live sports, ESPN+ content, channels and more
articles.summary: Here is everything sports fans need to know about the ESPN streaming service, including subscription plans, pricing, live sports, available channels, shows,...
articles.body:
ESPN has long been one of the biggest names in sports television, from live games and major events to daily studio shows like "SportsCenter," "First Take," and "Pardon the Interruption." But as more fans move away from traditional cable, ESPN has shifted its focus to streaming.

That evolution now runs through the ESPN app, which gives sports fans a more direct way to watch live games, studio programming, ESPN+ content, on-demand replays and more in one place. The updated platform includes multiple subscription options, headlined by ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited, with the latter designed for fans who want access to ESPN's full lineup of networks and services without relying only on a traditional TV package.

So, what does the ESPN app include, how is it different from ESPN+, and which plan makes the most sense for sports fans?

Here is everything you need to know about the ESPN app, including available plans, live sports coverage, streaming options and what subscribers get with each package.

The ESPN streaming service is the network's direct-to-consumer platform, built into the ESPN app. Instead of limiting access to fans with a traditional cable, satellite or live TV streaming subscription, ESPN now offers its own subscription plans that allow users to watch live sports, studio shows, original programming, highlights, replays and ESPN+ content in one place.

The service is designed to be a central hub for ESPN's sports coverage. Depending on the plan, subscribers can stream events and programming from ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPN on ABC, ESPN+, ESPN3, SEC Network+ and ACCNX. That means fans can use the ESPN app to follow everything from NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, and college football and college basketball to soccer, UFC, golf, tennis, documentaries and more.

The app also includes ESPN's daily studio programming, including shows like "SportsCenter," "First Take" and "College GameDay," along with on-demand replays, original series, personalized highlights and app features such as multiview on supported devices.

ESPN currently offers two main streaming tiers: ESPN Select , which is built around ESPN+ content, and ESPN Unlimited , which includes ESPN's full lineup of networks and services. For sports fans who want ESPN without relying only on a cable package, the ESPN app is now the main way to stream the network's live events and programming directly.

ESPN offers two main standalone subscription plans: ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited . The right choice depends on how much ESPN content you want to stream and whether you are looking for ESPN+ content only, or full access to ESPN's live TV networks.

ESPN Select is the lower-cost plan and is essentially the home for ESPN+ content. It includes live sports, on-demand replays, original shows, documentaries and other programming that has traditionally lived on ESPN+. It is a good option for fans who want select college sports, soccer, NHL games, golf, tennis, combat sports and ESPN originals, but do not need live streams of ESPN's full linear TV networks. ESPN lists the Select plan at $13.99 per month or $139.99 per year.

ESPN Unlimited is the more complete plan. It includes everything in ESPN Select, plus access to ESPN's full lineup of networks and services, including ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPN on ABC, ESPN3, SEC Network+, ACC Network Extra and ESPN+. For cord-cutters or fans who want the closest thing to a full ESPN TV package inside the ESPN app, Unlimited is the better fit. ESPN lists the Unlimited plan at $31.99 per month or $319.99 per year.

Here is a breakdown of what each ESPN subscription plan includes:

Features more than 30,000 live sporting events per year

Includes select college sports, international soccer, NHL, golf, tennis, combat sports, PLL and other events

Includes ESPN originals, documentaries, studio programming, on-demand replays and exclusive shows

Best for fans who want ESPN+ content but do not need live access to ESPN's cable networks

Adds live access to ESPN's full lineup of networks and services

Includes ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPN on ABC, ESPN3, SEC Network+ and ACCNX

Features more than 47,000 live events per year

Includes live games, studio shows, on-demand replays, documentaries, original programming and ESPN+ content

Best for fans who want the most complete ESPN streaming package without relying only on a traditional cable or satellite subscription

ESPN subscriptions can be purchased through the ESPN app or ESPN.com, and some fans may already have access to ESPN content through an eligible TV, mobile or live TV streaming provider. ESPN also offers bundle options with Disney+ and Hulu, so fans should compare standalone and bundle pricing before signing up.

ESPN promotions can change throughout the year, but subscribers currently have several ways to save by bundling ESPN with other streaming services instead of purchasing everything separately.

The main ESPN bundle is the Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Unlimited Bundle , which starts at $35.99 per month and includes Disney+ with ads, Hulu with ads and ESPN Unlimited. There is also a Premium version for $44.99 per month , which includes Disney+ and Hulu without ads, while ESPN Unlimited still includes ads in select live and linear programming. Both plans include access to ESPN's full lineup of networks and services, including ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, ESPN on ABC, ESPN+, SEC Network+ and ACCNX.

Fans who only need ESPN+ content can also choose a lower-cost bundle built around ESPN Select. The Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Select Bundle is listed at $21.99 per month , while the Premium version is $32.99 per month with ad-free Disney+ and Hulu . ESPN Select is the plan that includes ESPN+ content, but it does not include the full ESPN linear network lineup available with ESPN Unlimited.

There are also expanded sports bundles for fans who want more live event coverage. ESPN offers an ESPN and FOX One Bundle for $39.99 per month , giving subscribers ESPN Unlimited along with FOX's direct-to-consumer service, which includes FOX Sports, FS1, FS2, Big Ten Network and other FOX channels. ESPN also lists bundle options with NFL+ Premium , including ESPN Unlimited with NFL+ Premium for $39.99 per month , or Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Unlimited with NFL+ Premium starting at $45.99 per month .

Baseball fans may also find seasonal ESPN offers tied to MLB.TV . New subscribers who purchase MLB.TV can receive a one-month free trial of ESPN Unlimited , after which ESPN renews at the regular monthly price unless canceled. Existing ESPN Unlimited subscribers can also get a discounted MLB.TV seasonal plan for the 2026 MLB season.

For fans comparing all ESPN promotions , the best value depends on what they want to watch. ESPN Select is the cheaper option for ESPN+ content, ESPN Unlimited is the best standalone choice for ESPN's full network lineup, and the Disney+, Hulu and ESPN bundles are the strongest overall value for households that also want movies, shows and general entertainment in addition to live sports.

ESPN does not currently list a standard free trial for its standalone ESPN Select or ESPN Unlimited plans . ESPN's current subscription lists paid monthly and annual options for both plans, while ESPN also says there is no free trial for Disney+, Hulu and ESPN bundle plans . That means most fans should expect to choose a paid plan when signing up rather than starting with a free preview.

There are some exceptions for limited-time or partner-specific offers. For example, new subscribers who purchase MLB.TV through ESPN can receive a one-month free trial of ESPN Unlimited . After the trial period, ESPN Unlimited automatically renews at the regular monthly price unless the subscriber cancels or removes ESPN Unlimited from their account.

The good news for sports fans is that ESPN subscriptions are flexible. Subscribers can generally cancel ESPN at any time, making it easier to sign up around a specific season, tournament, playoff run or major event without a long-term contract. Fans should still check ESPN's latest offers before subscribing, because free trials, bundle discounts and seasonal promotions can change throughout the year.

What channels are on the ESPN streaming service?

The channels available on the ESPN streaming service depend on which plan you choose. ESPN Select is built around ESPN+ content, so it does not include live access to ESPN's full lineup of traditional TV networks. ESPN Unlimited is the more complete streaming plan and includes ESPN's linear channels, ESPN+ content and additional digital networks inside the ESPN app.

With ESPN Unlimited , subscribers can stream live games, studio shows, on-demand programming, replays and events from the following ESPN networks and services:

ESPN — The flagship network for major live games, studio shows and event coverage

ESPN2 — Additional live sports, studio programming and alternate broadcasts

ESPNU — College sports coverage, including football, basketball and Olympic sports

ESPNEWS — Sports news, highlights, analysis and overflow live event coverage

ESPN Deportes — Spanish-language ESPN coverage, including select live games and studio shows

SEC Network — SEC football, basketball, baseball, softball and other conference programming

ACC Network — ACC football, basketball, baseball, softball and other conference programming

ESPN+ — Live sports, original shows, documentaries and exclusive ESPN+ programming

ESPN on ABC — ESPN-produced games and events that air on ABC

ESPN3 — Digital live sports coverage and additional event streams

ACC Network Extra — Digital-only ACC live events and overflow coverage

For sports fans, the biggest difference is that ESPN Select is best for ESPN+ content , while ESPN Unlimited is designed to replace or supplement a full ESPN TV package . Unlimited is the better fit for fans who want access to ESPN's biggest live events, including NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, college football, college basketball, tennis, golf, WWE and postseason coverage across ESPN's networks.

ESPN is best known for live sports, but the ESPN app also includes a deep library of sports shows, documentaries, films, original series and on-demand programming. Subscribers can watch daily studio shows, event replays, highlight-driven programming and long-form storytelling from ESPN Films, making the service useful even when there is not a live game on. Its streaming library includes the 30 for 30 collection , ESPN Originals, news highlights, on-demand sports content and more.

The biggest draw for documentary fans is the complete 30 for 30 library , ESPN's award-winning sports documentary series. That collection includes classic films covering some of the most memorable athletes, teams, scandals and moments in sports history, from "You Don't Know Bo" and "The Two Escobars" to "Bad Boys," "Long Gone Summer" and other well-known titles. ESPN also continues to feature newer 30 for 30 releases alongside older classics.

ESPN subscribers can also stream original series built around some of the biggest names in sports. That includes storytelling franchises like "Peyton's Places" and "Eli's Places," plus athlete-focused documentaries and series such as "Man in the Arena: Tom Brady" and "In the Arena: Serena Williams." Availability can vary by plan, platform and bundle, but ESPN's on-demand library is designed to give fans more than just live games.

For fans comparing ESPN streaming plans, the on-demand library is one of the biggest reasons to consider the service beyond live sports. ESPN Select is built around ESPN+ content, including ESPN Originals and documentaries, while ESPN Unlimited adds the full ESPN network lineup for fans who also want live channels, major events and studio shows in the same app.

What sports are available to watch on ESPN?

ESPN's streaming sports lineup depends on which plan you choose and which events ESPN has the rights to carry. ESPN Select includes ESPN+ content only, while ESPN Unlimited includes ESPN+ plus ESPN's full lineup of networks and services, giving subscribers access to a much larger live sports schedule through the ESPN app. Select includes more than 30,000 live events per year, while Unlimited includes more than 47,000 live events per year.

That makes ESPN a strong option for fans who want live games, college sports, studio coverage, original programming and on-demand replays in one place. However, availability can vary by season, league, event, location and blackout rules, so fans should always check the ESPN schedule before signing up for a specific game.

UFC's live events moved to Paramount+ and CBS under a new rights deal, so fans looking specifically for UFC Fight Nights or numbered UFC events should not rely on ESPN as the main streaming home for those cards. All live UFC events in 2026 are on Paramount+.

For most fans, the easiest way to compare the plans is this: ESPN Select is best for ESPN+ live sports and originals, while ESPN Unlimited is best for fans who want ESPN's full live sports lineup, including events airing on ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPN on ABC, SEC Network, ACC Network and ESPN+.

How do I sign up for the ESPN streaming service?

Fans can sign up for the ESPN streaming service online through ESPN or inside the ESPN app. ESPN requires subscribers to create or log in with a MyDisney account, which is the same account system used across Disney+, Hulu and ESPN. From there, users can choose between ESPN Select, ESPN Unlimited or an eligible bundle, then enter payment information to start streaming.

Go to ESPN's streaming signup page Visit stream.espn.com or open the ESPN app on a supported device.

Fans who already receive ESPN through a cable, satellite or live TV streaming provider should check with their provider before signing up for a standalone plan. Some subscribers may already have access to ESPN content or may need to activate ESPN Unlimited through their TV provider account.

articles.title: Pirates' Brandon Lowe Explains Why Roberto Clemente Award Nomination is 'Special'
articles.summary: Having a career year, Brandon Lowe is honored to be nominated for an award named after a Pirates legend.
articles.body:
Roberto Clemente was one of the most beloved players in all of baseball. He represented the sport while with the Pirates , a historic franchise. His legacy after he passed lives on forever.

The Roberto Clemente Award is one of the most prestigious awards in baseball. Normally, being nominated would make any player proud. For the Pirates ' Brandon Lowe , wearing No. 21 on Roberto Clemente Day while being nominated meant the world to him.

"Yeah, I think there's a little more to it," Lowe said via TribLive , "being in Pittsburgh and seeing 21 on your jersey and everything that comes with that."

The Pirates traded for Brendan Lowe, Jake Magnum and Mason Montgomery during the 2025 MLB offseason. Lowe was coming off a career year in 2025 with the Rays, hitting 31 home runs with a .477 slugging percentage. In Pittsburgh, Lowe has had a season to remember.

Lowe has hit 30 home runs with a career-high 141 hits in 140 games. Lowe and Ryan O'Hearn became just the third duo in Pirates history to record 15+ home runs and 60+ RBIs before the All-Star break, joining Willie Stargell and Al Oliver (1973) and Barry Bonds and Bobby Bonilla (1990).

Off the field, Lowe hosts youth baseball players and continues his Home Runs for Hope campaign. He donates $250 to Pirates charities after every home run he hits, and has pledged money to various other organizations around Pittsburgh.

"It's a great example that he's (set) on the field and in the clubhouse, is the stability that he brings every single day, the professionalism and how he goes about it," Manager Don Kelly said about Lowe. "He shows up with the mindset every day to do whatever he can to help the team win. He shows that too in the community, showing up helping the team off the field, as well."

The last Pirates player to win the award was Andrew McCutchen in 2010. Before that? Willie Stargell in 1974. It's unknown if Lowe, a free agent next year, will win. But wearing a Pirates uniform while remembering Clemente is an honor he will never forget.

"The background of the award and everything the award stands for, obviously it's incredible," Lowe said. "There's a lot of people in this clubhouse that are doing a lot of things in this community, as well. To be able to be the nominee, especially in Pittsburgh, it does make it a little more special."

Following extended separations, Virginia and Virginia Tech each will reunite with a former ACC Coastal Division rival next football season.

The conference Wednesday unveiled league opponents for next year, and among the highlights are the Cavaliers' first game against Miami since 2023 and the Hokies' first contest versus North Carolina since 2022. Those four programs resided in the Coastal Division from 2005-22 — the 2020 pandemic season excepted — and played annually until the conference abandoned divisions for 2023 and beyond.

Schedule dates will be announced after this season, likely in late January. Virginia and Virginia Tech's 2027 ACC opponents are as follows.

Home: Louisville, Pitt, SMU, Virginia Tech.

Away: Boston College, Georgia Tech, Miami, North Carolina, Stanford.

Home: Clemson, Miami, NC State, Syracuse, Wake Forest.

The Hokies will complete their schedule with nonconference games against The Citadel, Liberty and Notre Dame. The Cavaliers have nonconference dates with Arkansas State and William & Mary but have not revealed their required Power Four opponent from outside the ACC.

Here's why: Georgia Tech plays nine ACC games next season but has nonconference dates on the books against Hampton, Tennessee, Notre Dame and Georgia. So, one of the four has to go.

Since Virginia needs a Power Four, simply swap Georgia Tech for UVA on Notre Dame's schedule.

Next season will mark the ACC's second with a nine-game conference schedule and its fourth since expanding to 17 teams by adding SMU, Cal and Stanford. The principles adopted for the 17-team model in 2024 remain: protected rivalries such as Virginia Tech-UVA, Virginia-North Carolina and Miami-Virginia Tech; Eastern time zone programs don't travel to California in consecutive seasons; teams play at least twice every seven seasons.

In shifting to a nine-game model, the ACC required at least one nonconference date with a Power Four peer or independent Notre Dame. To make the scheduling math work, one ACC team each year will play eight league games — that's Clemson in 2027 — and must play two Power Fours/Notre Dame.

After months of conversations, ACC athletic directors approved the 2027 schedule during in-person meetings last week at conference headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina. articles.title: David Pollack asks for prayers as his wife faces a third surgery
articles.summary: Former Georgia Bulldogs star David Pollack says his wife Lindsey needs a third surgery following her brain cancer diagnosis
articles.body:
Former Georgia Bulldogs defensive end and college football analyst David Pollack shared an unfortunate news update on his wife via social media.

"We didn't get the best news today at a doctors visit," Pollack said. Pollack's wife, Lindsey, has previously been diagnosed with brain cancer and has already undergone multiple surgeries. Pollack shares that she needs a third surgery.

"She looked at me and said God has been building me for this, and thank goodness its on a bye week so Nicholas doesn't have a game," Pollack continued.

His son, Nicholas, is committed to playing college football at an ACC powerhouse and plays high school football for North Oconee, which is located close to Athens, Georgia . It appears that his wife's surgery will be sometime around Friday, Sept. 25, which is when North Oconee has its bye week. North Oconee is 4-1 to start the 2026 high school season.

"She is weak right now, but our God isn't," Pollack adds. "If you are the praying type we will take 'em all."

In March, Pollack shared that his wife was "cancer-free" after battling for over a year.

Pollack himself underwent a major surgery to repair a broken neck injury he suffered in 2006. Pollack's severe injury derailed his promising NFL career and forced him to retire from football. David and Lindsey Pollack have the support of many folks during this tough time.

Pollack continues to cover college football with On3 after his departure from ESPN's "College GameDay." Pollack and his wife both founded The Pollack Foundation , which seeks to improve the lives of families in the Atlanta and Athens areas in Georgia.

articles.body:
Manchester United head coach may have inadvertently played a role in alienating the club's teenage jewel, JJ Gabriel.

The 15-year-old is widely considered the most exciting English player of his age . After conquering the under-18s level last season, he was promoted to the under-21s this season.

Sadly for MUFC supporters, they received shocking news on Tuesday, as it was revealed that Gabriel has requested his departure .

Did Carrick's choices prompt JJ Gabriel desire to leave?

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

In his latest piece for the BBC , Man Utd correspondent Simon Stone delved into the situation.

The veteran journalist revealed that United have the young forward under a scholarship contract until the end of the season (as he remains too young to sign a professional contract), but he is allowed to leave the club to join a foreign club in October thanks to his European Union passport.

JJ hails from an Irish father (of Trinidad and Tobago heritage) and a Greek-Cypriot mother.

The report also revealed that Gabriel and his entourage were left irritated by some of the promises that weren't fulfilled.

The striker has been occasionally training with the first team since Ruben Amorim's reign, but he was expected to earn more playing time in pre-season than the few minutes he received against Atletico Madrid .

Gabriel was also disgruntled about being left out in favour of 18-year-old Tynan Thompson, who was played 45 minutes in the friendly against Leeds United , despite having only arrived at the club.

Stone adds that the final straw may have been the teenager's Champions League exclusion. Due to his tender age, Gabriel would have only been eligible to play in the UEFA competition had the club registered him on its A list.

That would have allowed him to feature in the 4-0 victory over Sabah, especially when the game was sealed in the second half.

However, Carrick inexplicably selected Manuel Ugarte instead, even though the Uruguayan will remain on the sidelines for the bulk of the campaign.

It should be noted that the registration window opens again in January, meaning that the manager could have kept Ugarte out of the squad during the first half of the season, before reintroducing him later in the campaign.

Is Man Utd's slow & steady approach justified?

At this stage, it appears that United and Gabriel's entourage have contrasting opinions regarding the timing and pace.

While the teenager feels he's ready for prime time, the club is reluctant to thrust him into the action, believing he has yet to reach the required physical level.

Perhaps each side has a valid point, but the issue for Man Utd is that the player and his family hold all the cards due to the lack of a professional contract.

So unless INEOS can somehow convince Gabriel that staying at Carrington is in his best interest, the fans should brace themselves for some dire news in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Oregon In Trouble? UCLA Turning Heads? Klatt Names Alarming, Exciting CFB Teams
articles.summary: FOX Sports' Joel Klatt reacts to which teams need to panic, stay calm or get excited after Week 2.
articles.body: Week 2 of the college football season was nothing but thrilling. Oregon and Oklahoma faced massive upsets, Texas claimed the No. 1 spot in the rankings and Bob Chesney and UCLA are continuing to prove their offseason hype in the regular season. Notably, Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor defeated its first Big Ten opponent on the road for the first time since 1980. But after two weeks, where do some teams sit in terms of their outlook on the rest of the year? On "The Joel Klatt Show," FOX Sports' Joel Klatt broke down teams that fall into three categories: Time to panic, stay calm and get excited. Time To Panic Oregon Ducks Klatt's thoughts: "If not for those two defensive scores, that is a route. A route! The film was alarming for Oregon. On both sides of the ball. I think it's time to panic. It's not just the result, now they're dealing with some injury issues… Injuries are always going to happen, there's no doubt, but you don't want them to happen when you're trying to right the ship. "I was on a deep dive in both last year's film from Oregon, and this year against Boise State, and what did I find? Oregon has run-pass tells in their offense, and this is a devastating deal… but the film was also alarming on the defensive side." Oklahoma Sooners Klatt's thoughts: "Oklahoma doesn't have an offensive line and they cannot run the football. And in order to move the ball, John Mateer has to be Superman, or they've got to create explosive plays. And they couldn't do either of those things against Michigan last week. Can you really rely on splash explosive plays the entire season? I don't think you can, it's ultimately what their Achilles heel was a year ago." Washington Huskies Klatt's thoughts: "Washington barely snuck out a win against Utah State, 16-14 last week. The offense has not clicked, and that's where Jed Fish's experience and expertise lies. And yeah they're 2-0, but I'm sitting here looking at their schedule and I'm like, ‘Oh I don’t know about this.' "The offense has been hit by a ton of injuries right now. They lost their top two running backs. They lost wide receiver Christian Moss to a leg injury. Starting wide receiver Rashid Williams, he's week to week… they're banged up right now." Florida State Klatt's thoughts: "Does ‘panic’ encapsulate Florida State? I don't think it does. Fired their athletic director on Monday – by the way that was the same guy who gave Mike Norvell his extension, so handwriting is on the wall there. The athletic department finished the 2025 fiscal year with $437 million of debt. Yikes. "The debt thing is a big deal, because if you fire Mike Norvell in the middle of the year you're going to owe him $50 million… it would be roughly $800,000 a month until 2031… I bring all of that up because this roster is limited, reportedly it's in the bottom half of the ACC as far as funding goes. They're 3-14 in their last 17 ACC games. And look at their next four games against Power 4 opponents – this is like panic, panic, panic: at Alabama this weekend in Tuscaloosa; Virginia, which is a good team, they're ranked; Louisville, which is a very good team, almost beat Ole Miss; and at Miami, who we think is one of the best teams in the country." Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets Klatt's thoughts: "Time to panic. They were 8-0 last year at one point behind Haynes King. Now all of a sudden, they've lost six of their last seven. Their only win was a fourth quarter comeback against Boston College. I don't love that. I don't love the trajectory that's going on at Georgia Tech. I just don't. It's time to panic there." Stay Calm Colorado Buffaloes Klatt's thoughts: "I think it would be easy to get excited based on the way that Colorado ran the ball against Georgia Tech, the way that they threw the ball last week against, granted, FCS Weber State, but this looks different. This looks a lot more real than any of the versions of Colorado. You see their nine-win team with Travis Hunter, Heisman trophy winner and Shedeur Sanders at quarterback – they largely just had elite, upper-level skill position players, and then got by everywhere else. This looks a lot more fundamentally sound. "They changed their philosophy over the offseason. They went from trying to go after splash recruiting and roster building to production over potential roster building, and it shows. They're a lot tougher on the line of scrimmage, their defense can actually play up front, they're committed to the run – they do it with a tight end and a fullback at times, which I really love that physical aspect of the run game." Ohio State Buckeyes Klatt's thoughts: "Let's all relax about Ohio State. Would they have liked to win that game? Obviously. Were they in position to win that game? Yes… Let's just take a bit of a chill pill, can we? I mean this is a team that was dominating Texas in their building for three quarters, basically. Are they going to be ok? Yes, they are going to be ok. Mainly, the one they've got to get fixed is the fact that their defense was exposed late to volume. That's what happened… What killed Ohio State was the fact that their defense was on the field for the entire fourth quarter and part of the third. So what's the fix? Well. you've got to figure out the red zone. They're going to have to find a run game in the red zone, and find ways to execute better in the red zone." BYU Cougars Klatt's thoughts: "Cautiously optimistic about BYU. I think that they are very good, but what we don't know is can they level up? We've seen this before. I know Bear Bachmeier is a grinder and he's a good player. I know LJ Martin is a good player. I know you're going to play solid defense. I know all these things – I know you're going to beat teams that are at your level or below. "I don't know what to make of BYU at that level until they play Notre Dame, until they play a Texas Tech." Alabama Crimson Tide Klatt's thoughts: "I'm going to stay calm. Let's let Keelon Russell get good at quarterback. I wanted to get excited about them, and not because of Russell and not even because their defense was dominant against Kentucky… this other element showed up in the second half against Kentucky…they stayed committed to the run game…and they ran for over 150 yards. Now that's a blueprint, a blueprint that allows you to keep the pressure off of your young quarterback. He's going to continue to get better. "I'm cautiously optimistic about Alabama… I think they've got real high potential, a high ceiling if they can run it, bring their quarterback along, and allow him to be explosive both in the pass game and in the run game down the stretch. USC Trojans Klatt's thoughts: "The freshman are really good, I love what they've got going out there. At wide receiver, Trent Mosley is a star, Kayden Dixon-Wyatt is very good. Their tight end, Mark Bowman, he's excellent. Luke Wafle, their defensive end, is one of the better freshmen defensive ends that I've seen in a long time – he creates havoc in the backfield. And this is looking like what Lincoln Riley told us about over the course of the offseason. "But I'm going to be cautious with this one, and the reason is I still want to see it from a defensive perspective against better competition. I still need to see them play well, get after the quarterback and more specifically stop the run in a big matchup-style game." Get Excited UCLA Bruins Klatt's thoughts: "I'm excited about UCLA. Now, this doesn't mean I think they're going to the playoff. This means that, if I'm a UCLA fan, I am thrilled with how this season has started. You've got an experienced quarterback in Nico Iamaleava…Wayne Knight has been tremendous… (Bob) Chesney knows what he's doing. He brought that entire staff, he brought all that core of players, this is a team that I think is going to knock somebody off in the Big Ten that we don't expect them to knock off in the Big Ten. That's a real team." Miami (Fla.) Hurricanes Klatt's thoughts: "I am absolutely thrilled and excited about Miami. I think they're better than they were a year ago. Here's the thing that I'm going to hang my hat on: Darian Mensah looks like an upgrade at quarterback from Carson Beck. He looks dynamic, and that's scary because they're still dominating at the offensive line level. "They're still dominating at the defensive line. That's the DNA of their program, they've recruited very well… the one thing that gets me the most excited: Malachi Toney. Malachi Toney is an absolute cheat code. He is phenomenal, you can get him the ball anywhere and he can dominate a game." Texas Longhorns Klatt's thoughts: "Yeah it was sloppy for Texas, but I'm excited about Texas. If I'm a Longhorn fan today, I am fired up. Why? Because the ceiling has now been lifted off of my program. [Coach Steve] Sarkisian said it himself in the postgame presser: ‘Now we know we can.’ That was the most important comment, from any coach, across America on Saturday. "What's more dangerous than a talented team? A talented team that believes. And now Texas believes. It wasn't pretty. In fact, they're watching the film thinking to themselves, ‘We should have won that by more.’ … I'm excited about those backs. Woo! Those backs can run, man." Michigan Wolverines Klatt's thoughts: "You could tell me, ‘No, no, no, Joel, you need to stay calm.' I’m not going to stay calm, I'm going to get excited about Michigan. And here's the reason why: they won Kyle Whittingham's way. His DNA was all over that field. He won the tug of war. "New coaches have to go in and win the culture of that locker room. And to win the locker room over, you've got to be more steadfast than the locker room. And that's what that win did for them against Oklahoma. They did it with man coverage – that's Kyle Whittingham. They did it with great pass rush. That's Kyle Whittingham. And they did it running the quarterback, being rugged on offense. That's. Kyle. Whittingham." Mississippi State Bulldogs Klatt's thoughts: "I am excited about Mississippi State, and I think you should be too. They're quietly out there. They went up there and hammered Minnesota, and that's not a bad Minnesota team… That's a really good win for Jeff Lebby and Mississippi State. I love their quarterback, Kamario Taylor. He's the new star on the block. This kid can throw it, he's athletic. He's big, 6-foot-4, 230 pounds. He's mobile, he's got an absolute cannon. This kid executes this system really well. "They will beat someone that raises your eyebrows in the SEC this year. I'm excited about Mississippi State this year. I really like them. Defense is playing well. In particular, last week didn't allow an offensive touchdown against Minnesota." articles.title: Ander Martín, Esther Briz y el resto de españoles brillan en el inicio del Europeo de beach sprint
articles.standfirst: Habrá presencia española en los cuartos de solo y doble mixto, tanto en categoría absoluta como sub 19
articles.summary: Habrá presencia española en los cuartos de solo y doble mixto, tanto en categoría absoluta como sub 19
articles.body: Los Campeonatos de Europa de remo de mar y beach sprint dieron comienzo en las aguas de La Línea de la Concepción (Cádiz), donde se reúnen 1.200 deportistas procedentes de 31 países. Después de las jornadas previas de entrenamientos y la ceremonia inaugural, la competición en sí ya ha arrancado en la Playa de Poniente, escenario durante las dos primeras jornadas de las pruebas de velocidad. La prueba continental de beach sprint, disciplina que se estrenará en el programa de los Juegos Olímpicos en Los Ángeles 2028 y que combina carreras a pie en la orilla con un recorrido balizado en el agua de 500 metros, con enfrentamientos directos entre dos embarcaciones, ha asumido el protagonismo en el arranque. Lo ha hecho con la presencia de 137 embarcaciones procedentes de 31 países, repartidas en siete modalidades. Con participación española en todas las disciplinas (sólo masculino y femenino y doble mixto, tanto absoluto como sub19; y doble mixto inclusivo), la jornada inaugural ha estado reservada a las tomas de tiempos o time trials, que han servido para definir los primeros clasificados para las eliminatorias, que arrancaban en la sesión de tarde con los duelos de octavos de final. A destacar la gran puesta en escena de la selección española, que confirmando sus opciones de podio lograba los mejores tiempos de todos los participantes en seis de las siete categorías, siendo segunda en la restante para pasar directamente a la primera ronda eliminatoria sin tener que acudir a los segundos time trial. Ya en la sesión de tarde, en la que el viento y el oleaje añadieron un punto de complejidad extra a la competición, tampoco fallaron los anfitriones en los octavos de final, accediendo en solo juvenil, a costa de los representantes de Lituania e Irlanda, los alicantinos Xavier Torres (S.D. Club Náutico Santa Pola) y Marina López (R.C. Regatas de Alicante). Posteriormente lo hicieron en la categoría absoluta los solos del también alicantino Ander Martín (R.C. Náutico Torrevieja) y la aragonesa Esther Briz (R.C. Náutico Torrevieja), en ambos casos ante deportistas de Estonia. En doble mixto, el local Alfredo Mena (Club Remo de Mar La Línea) y la murciana Blanca López (Club Náutico Santa Lucía) superaron el primer knockout sub19 ante Portugal, mientras que Miguel Salas (R.C. Regatas de Alicante) y la malagueña Teresa Díaz (R.C. Mediterráneo) tendrán que esperar a la apertura de la jornada este jueves (8:30 h) en la categoría absoluta ante Suecia tras no haber luz suficiente para cerrar la ronda de octavos en la primera jornada. Decididos por tanto los botes aspirantes definitivos a las medallas, el Europeo de beach sprint 2026 concluye este jueves en La Línea con la celebración de las distintas fases finales, a disputar desde las 9:00 horas a partir de cuartos de final a excepción del doble mixto inclusivo, con sólo dos tripulaciones inscritas. En este sentido, España optará al título ante Gran Bretaña en final directa prevista a las 12:20 h con la gallega Rocío Fraguela (Club Mar de Noia) y el malagueño Marcos Delgado (Real Club Mediterráneo), que podrán elegir calle al imponerse este miércoles en la regata previa. El programa del día arrancará a las 8:30 h con los octavos del doble mixto pendiente para dar paso a las rondas finales de solo juvenil masculino (9:00 h) y femenino (9:50 h), pruebas a las que seguirán las de solo absoluto masculino (10:40 h) y femenino (11:30 h) para concluir, tras la final del doble inclusivo, con los cuartos, semis y finales B y A de los dobles mixtos sub19 (12:40 h) y absoluto (13:30 h). Tras las finales, se celebrará la entrega de medallas a partir de las 15:00 horas para dar paso a los entrenamientos del Europeo de remo de mar o resistencia, a celebrar de viernes a domingo de forma paralela al Campeonato de España de la modalidad.
