articles.title: El intento desesperado de Lorenzo por retener a James antes de anunciar su retiro de la Selección
articles.standfirst: La llamada secreta entre Néstor Lorenzo y James Rodríguez del anuncio oficial de su renuncia a la Selección Colombia
articles.summary: La llamada secreta entre Néstor Lorenzo y James Rodríguez del anuncio oficial de su renuncia a la Selección Colombia
articles.body: El fútbol colombiano vive días de profunda conmoción tras confirmarse el fin de una era en el combinado nacional. James Rodríguez, el gran referente y capitán del equipo durante la última década y media, anunció oficialmente que da un paso al costado y no volverá a vestir la camiseta tricolor. Sin embargo, tras la conmoción inicial provocada por el comunicado del volante cucuteño, se han empezado a revelar detalles inéditos sobre los momentos previos a la decisión, incluyendo una conversación privada e intensa entre el futbolista y el director técnico Néstor Lorenzo. La noticia del retiro de James Rodríguez a sus 35 años tomó por sorpresa a gran parte de la afición y a la propia Federación Colombiana de Fútbol. Con las fechas FIFA de septiembre y octubre a la vuelta de la esquina, el estratega Néstor Lorenzo intentó por todos los medios evitar que su máximo baluarte dentro del campo hiciera pública su salida. Según reveló el periodista Eduardo Luis López en La FM, citando fuentes cercanas al entorno del mediocampista, existió un diálogo directo entre el director técnico y el jugador antes de que este publicara su mensaje de despedida. En dicho intercambio, Lorenzo fue enfático y suplicó al capitán que reconsiderara su posición: "Lorenzo le dijo 'no lo hagas'", detalló el periodista sobre la llamada en la que el DT argentino intentó frenar el anuncio del volante zurdo. Lorenzo, quien asumió el banquillo de la Selección en 2022 y logró revivir la mejor versión del '10' —llevándolo a ser una de las grandes figuras de la Copa América—, consideraba que James aún tenía fútbol y liderazgo que aportar en el nuevo proceso rumbo a los próximos retos internacionales. A pesar de los intentos del seleccionador por convencerlo, James Rodríguez mantuvo firme su postura. A través de un emotivo video de más de tres minutos de duración compartido en sus redes sociales, el cucuteño repasó los momentos más icónicos de su trayectoria con la Selección y confirmó que su ciclo con el equipo patrio había llegado a su fin. "Hoy quiero hablarles desde el corazón. Después de muchos años, muchos partidos, muchas alegrías y también momentos duros, siento que llegó el momento de cerrar una de las etapas más importantes de mi vida, mi camino con la Selección Colombia", expresó el futbolista en el video. El exjugador del Real Madrid y Bayern Múnich reflexionó sobre lo que significó portar la cinta de capitán y llevar el número 10 en la espalda: "Vestir esta camiseta fue un sueño, pero también una responsabilidad enorme. Cada vez que entré a una cancha entendí que no solo jugaba por mí, jugaba por mi familia, mis compañeros y por millones de colombianos que soñaban con nosotros". La salida de James deja un vacío inmenso en el esquema táctico del entrenador argentino. La FCF recientemente renovó el contrato de Néstor Lorenzo con la misión de comandar la transición y renovación generacional del plantel, un pedido recurrente por parte de diversos sectores de la prensa y la hinchada. El estratega entregará en las próximas horas la lista de convocados para la gira de tres amistosos contra México, Paraguay y Perú en el marco de una fecha FIFA extendida de tres semanas. Estos compromisos servirán como el primer banco de pruebas para evaluar quiénes asumirán la responsabilidad de la creación de juego y el liderazgo en la era posterior a James Rodríguez.

articles.title: 49ers WR De’Zhaun Stribling Undergoes Ankle Surgery, Could Miss Up To 10 Weeks
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are officially placing wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
articles.body: The injury bug strikes the San Francisco 49ers yet again. San Francisco 49ers rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling is reportedly expected to miss at least two months after undergoing surgery on his injured left ankle. Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that he opted for surgery and added he expected Stribling to miss about 10 weeks. On Wednesday morning, ESPN reported that 49ers rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling is expected to miss at least a month after injuring his ankle in Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams. The 49ers then officially placed Stribling on injured reserve, which will meant he would miss at least four games. Stribling’s absence is another blow to a wide receiver unit already missing Ricky Pearsall, who is out for the season with a knee injury. Stribling, a second-round pick out of Ole Miss, suffered an ankle injury late in the first quarter against the Rams but returned to action. His return was brief, however, as he went down again on the 49ers' next drive and had to be carted off the field. While there was initial speculation of an Achilles tear, head coach Kyle Shanahan ruled that out after the game. Stribling's impact in his NFL debut was limited, but the 49ers were still able to pull out a win against their divisional opponent. The passing attack didn’t miss a beat, as quarterback Brock Purdy put together a strong performance. Though Stribling failed to record a catch in the season opener, he had a strong offseason and training camp for the 49ers. With him sidelined, expect an increased workload for veteran receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson. Against the Rams, the trio combined for 14 catches for 147 yards and three touchdowns. The 49ers host the Miami Dolphins in Week 2. How the San Francisco offense maintains its explosiveness will be something to watch.

articles.title: Yankees RHP Clarke Schmidt Returns As Reliever After 14-Month Rehab
articles.summary: The Yankees returned right-hander Clarke Schmidt from the injured list with an aim to integrate him into their bullpen for the postseason.
articles.body: The New York Yankees returned right-handed pitcher Clarke Schmidt from his rehabilitation assignment and reinstated him from the injured list on Wednesday, aiming to integrate the 30-year-old into their bullpen for the postseason following his 14-month recovery from elbow surgery. Schmidt had an internal brace procedure on his ulnar collateral ligament on July 11, 2025, and began minor league rehab on Aug. 29. The 2017 first-round draft pick was used exclusively as a starter since 2023, but with Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Carlos Rodon and Gerrit Cole in the rotation, Schmidt will transition to relief. "It's been a long journey, a lot of work that goes into this. A lot of long days, early mornings," Schmidt said before the game Wednesday against the Minnesota Twins. "I've just been itching to come back." The Yankees designated popular multi-position player Oswaldo Cabrera for assignment to make room on the 40-man roster for Schmidt. Cabrera missed most of the 2025 season with a severe ankle injury. "I’m blessed to have a lot of guys on this team that you just admire and respect and love doing the job with on a daily basis," manager Aaron Boone said. "Oswaldo’s right there at the top of that list." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Seahawks Coach Mike Macdonald Declares QB Sam Darnold Week 2 Status
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald ruled out quarterback Sam Darnold (glute) for their Week 2 road game against the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body: It will be a no-go for Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald revealed in a press conference on Wednesday afternoon that Darnold won't dress for the team's Week 2 road matchup against the Arizona Cardinals due to the glute injury he sustained in the team's Week 1 win over the New England Patriots. Darnold suffered the injury on the Seahawks' opening possession of the season and was replaced at quarterback by Drew Lock, who will get the starting nod against the Cardinals. Macdonald said Seattle doesn't "anticipate" placing Darnold on injured reserve. Darnold reportedly suffered a muscle strain but not a fracture, giving the Seahawks optimism that the starting quarterback's absence will be short-lived. Taking over in the first quarter for Darnold against the Patriots, Lock threw for 187 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions, while posting a 113.3 passer rating and completing 72.7% of his passes (16 of 22) in a 13-10 win for the Seahawks. Behind Lock, who has 28 NFL starts under his belt, is second-year quarterback and former third-round pick Jalen Milroe. Last season (2025), Darnold totaled 4,048 passing yards, 25 passing touchdowns, 14 interceptions and a 99.1 passer rating, while completing 67.7% of his passes in what was his first year with the Seahawks. He also earned his second consecutive Pro Bowl nod. And, of course, the 2025 campaign, which saw Seattle have the best record in the NFC at 14-3, concluded with Darnold, Macdonald and the Seahawks winning Super Bowl LX, the second championship triumph in franchise history. As for Seattle's Week 2 game against Arizona, which can be viewed on Sunday afternoon at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX, the Seahawks swept the 2025 season series with their NFC West rival and have won nine consecutive games against the Cardinals.

articles.title: Five things to watch for in Dolphins at 49ers on Sunday
articles.summary: It’s Week 2 for the Miami Dolphins rebuild and we’ll soon see how quickly one-week regular-season progress can be made as the low-expectation Dolphins (0-1)...
articles.body:
It's Week 2 for the Miami Dolphins rebuild and we'll soon see how quickly one-week regular-season progress can be made as the low-expectation Dolphins (0-1) visit the high-expectation San Francisco 49ers (1-0) on Sunday, and the Dolphins have lots of areas for improvement .

Few think the Dolphins will win this game — they started the week as 13 1/2-point underdogs, which is an extreme margin in the NFL — but Miami should be able to shore up some things that went wrong in last Sunday's 27-13 loss at the Las Vegas Raiders .

Here are five things to watch for in Sunday's game:

We'll see how much Miami's top coaches — head coach Jeff Hafley, offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik, defensive coordinator Sean Duggan and special teams coordinator Chris Tabor — learned about their players last Sunday, and whether they're able to apply that knowledge this week. Players were OK on Xs and Os against the Raiders but in areas such as physicality, tackling, special team assignments, pass coverage and penalties there were numerous errors.

That's understandable. It was Week 1 of a rebuild with a young roster. The important thing is how the coaches guide their players from here. There should be one or two areas of tangible improvement this week, and if not it'll reflect poorly on the coaching.

Run game and run defense success gets into physicality, a major demand from Hafley. The Dolphins rushed for 74 yards on 18 carries and allowed Las Vegas to rush for 130 yards on 37 carries.

Both are bad for a few reasons. Running back De'Von Achane (36 yards on 11 carries) had few holes to run through. That must change and that starts with the offensive line, led by All Pro center Aaron Brewer , rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor and left tackle Patrick Paul , blowing open some holes. San Francisco allowed 122 rushing yards to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1, so there's hope for Miami's run game to gain some yards and have sustained drives.

Defensively, the Dolphins must be careful because San Francisco rushed for 174 yards last week led by running back Christian McCaffrey's 68 yards and Kaelon Black's 65 yards. The Dolphins' front seven, led by defensive tackle Zach Sieler , All Pro linebacker Jordyn Brooks (11 tackles) and rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez (14 tackles, second in the NFL), must be better.

Quarterback Malik Willis (15 of 27, 220 yards, no touchdowns, one interception, 66.9 passer rating) was so-so in his debut . He made good decisions and didn't repeat mistakes, but this week he must advance to making things happen with his legs and right arm. Willis doesn't need to play reckless football but he needs to push the envelope a bit in an effort to find out things about himself and his teammates.

Perhaps Willis needs to throw a pass into a tight window to one of his rookie wide receivers, Caleb Douglas or Chris Bell, as opposed to making the safe pass to sure-handed slot receiver Malik Washington . Again, don't play recklessly, which can lead to turnovers. Rather, take a chance once or twice. This is more about discovery than taking needless risks. But it's a fine line that Willis needs to toe.

This applies offensively, defensively, on special teams, in the locker room, on the bus, in practice, and everywhere else. Physicality can't be stressed enough. This team, above all else this season, must establish an identity, an unyielding quality that exists, win or lose, and Hafley and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan have decreed that quality will be physicality.

Hafley said the Dolphins were a bit timid to open the Raiders game. So let's see the physicality this week for the entire game. By the way, this is an area in which the three "pillars" of the rebuild — Achane, Brewer and Brooks along with the team captains — need to energize their teammates.

Who has more tackles — Patterson or Robinson?

Kicker Riley Patterson had two tackles vs. the Raiders while edge rusher Chop Robinson had one . Obviously something is wrong there, and if that repeats it might be an indication of major problems. Robinson, the training camp MVP selection by numerous media outlets, was quiet against the run and pass against Las Vegas. He must come alive in both ways this week the way he did in training camp. The Dolphins need his talent and energy.

Special teams was a troubling area during the Raiders game among allowing two long kickoff returns (45 and 50 yards, Patterson had the tackle on both) that led to touchdowns, a long punt return (23 yards), and missing a 41-yard field goal attempt that might have been tipped. Yes, kickoff returner Jaylen Wright had a 79-yarder but the Dolphins didn't score due to the missed field goal attempt. Special teams must be better this week on both handling their assignments and making tackles.

articles.title: Sam Darnold Injury Update Gives Seahawks Clearer Picture Ahead of Week 2 Matchup
articles.summary: Sam Darnold’s debut with the Seattle Seahawks got off to a rough start after he was forced to exit their Week 1 matchup against the New England Patriots earl...
articles.body:
Sam Darnold 's debut with the Seattle Seahawks got off to a rough start after he was forced to exit their Week 1 matchup against the New England Patriots early due to injury.

While further evaluation has since confirmed he will miss Week 2, there is some optimism that he could return as early as Week 3.

Sam Darnold's injury keeps him out of Week 2

Sam Darnold will miss the Seattle Seahawks ' Week 2 game after suffering an injury early in their Week 1 matchup against the New England Patriots. During Seattle's opening offensive series, Patriots defensive lineman Dre'Mont Jones sacked Darnold for a 5-yard loss. Darnold came up limping after the play, went to the sideline for evaluation and did not return to the game.

Darnold completed one of his two pass attempts for 13 yards before leaving the game. Drew Lock took over at quarterback after Darnold left and finished the game for Seattle .

The injury was initially reported as a hip issue . Further testing later showed that Darnold had a soft-tissue injury in his glute, while his hip joint was fine. Initial tests also ruled out a fracture.

NFL insider Ian Rapoport provided the latest update on 'The Pat McAfee Show', saying Darnold will miss Week 2 but still has a chance to return for Seattle's Week 3 matchup. He said , "Sam Darnold isn't gonna play this week. The Commanders game in week 3 is 17 days from when the Seahawks played. There's at least a chance that he plays in that game."

Seattle will reassess his status ahead of Week 3. Early evaluations suggest the injury may not keep him sidelined for an extended period. Seattle will turn to Drew Lock against Arizona while monitoring Darnold's recovery.

Drew Lock starts as Sam Darnold remains out

Drew Lock will have a full week to prepare as the Seattle Seahawks' starting quarterback for Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals . He entered the Week 1 game against the New England Patriots after Sam Darnold suffered an injury and took over for the rest of the game. Lock helped the Seahawks rally for a 13-10 win.

Lock completed 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. He also posted a 113.3 passer rating. His biggest play came in the fourth quarter, when he connected with Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 45-yard touchdown that helped Seattle get back into the game.

Unlike Week 1, Lock enters this matchup with starter reps throughout the week. The Seahawks will face the Cardinals in Week 2, with Lock set to lead the offense from the opening snap.

Seattle's medical staff will continue monitoring Darnold's recovery in the coming days, and any increase in his on-field workload would be an encouraging sign for the quarterback. The extended gap before Seattle's Week 3 matchup also gives him additional time to progress through treatment without the team needing to rush his return.

Cleveland Browns WR Jerry Jeudy (wrist) fully participated in practice Wednesday, Sept. 16.

articles.summary: Tom Izzo and Michigan State basketball now knows their 2026-27 Big Ten schedule to try and deliver Izzo a record 12th regular-season conference title.
articles.body:
The path to a Big Ten championship is set and will require Michigan State basketball to get through the defending national champs, with the hope that ultimately leads Tom Izzo back to Detroit and another Final Four.

The conference released its 2026-27 schedule Wednesday, Sept. 16. And Spartans know they will face Michigan twice, first in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Feb. 13 and then later in East Lansing on Friday, Feb. 26.

Izzo, who owns 11 regular season conference championships, will be looking to break a tie with Bob Knight and Ward "Piggy" Lambert for the most in Big Ten history. MSU won the Big Ten most recently in 2025 en route to an Elite Eight appearance.

The Spartans went 27-8 overall last season and made the Sweet 16 for third time in the past four years, finishing at 15-5 and in a three-way tie for second in Big Ten play after winning the league title the previous year. The postseason league tournament returns to Indianapolis from March 9–14.

The Wolverines and former coach Dusty May swept MSU last winter, 83-71 at Breslin Center and 90-80 at Crisler Center. U-M ran away with the Big Ten title and captured its first national title since 1989 in April.

Entering his 32nd season as the Spartans' head coach, Izzo is looking for his second national title to go with the one he won in 2000 and trying to get to his first Final Four since 2019, which was his eighth. MSU also is the host school for the 2027 Final Four at Ford Field on April 3 and 5 .

Along with playing defending Big Ten champ Michigan in the annual rivalry two-play, MSU will face Maryland and Nebraska both at Breslin Center and on the road.

The Spartans' home one-play opponents will be Minnesota, Oregon, Penn State, Purdue, Rutgers, Washington and Wisconsin. Their road-only games will be at Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Nebraska, Ohio State, UCLA and USC.

The games at USC and UCLA mark the second Los Angeles trip in three years since the Big Ten expanded to 18 teams in 2024-25. The Spartans will welcome Washington and Oregon after traveling to the Pacific Northwest last season.

DETROIT (AP) — The Detroit Lions will be without two starting offensive linemen against the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night.

Detroit ruled out rookie offensive tackle Blake Miller (knee) and guard Christian Mahogany (hip) with injuries. Cornerback D.J. Reed (foot) was questionable on the injury report Wednesday.

Miller, drafted No. 17 overall after not missing a game at Clemson, played through a knee injury during his NFL debut in an overtime win over New Orleans on Sunday. Mahogany was hurt early in the game against the Saints .

The Lions have veterans to fill in for Miller and Mahogany, who was replaced by 28-year-old Ben Bartch against the Saints. Larry Borom , who has 38 career starts, will likely start at right tackle in place of Miller against the Bills.

Detroit's top free agent addition, center Cade Mays , went on injured reserve nearly a month ago with a wrist injury.

articles.title: Drake Maye Admits Patriots’ Long Layoff Made Week 1 Loss Tougher To Shake
articles.summary: Drake Maye explained why the Patriots’ extended layoff made their season-opening loss linger and identified the mistakes New England must correct immediately...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots had more time than usual to process everything that went wrong in their season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks .

Quarterback Drake Maye is not convinced that was necessarily helpful. New England opened its season Wednesday night, giving the Patriots several extra days before beginning preparations for their Week 2 matchup. Instead of quickly returning to the facility and shifting his attention to another opponent, Maye had an entire weekend to replay the frustrating moments from the 13-10 loss.

"It's tough," Maye told reporters. "You have a lot of time to think about it."

Maye usually follows the NFL's unofficial 24-hour rule. He evaluates the previous game, learns from it and then attempts to move forward. The unusual Wednesday opener disrupted that routine.

"I think that definitely over the weekend, you're watching it and thinking about it," Maye said. "Usually, I have kind of the 24 hours. You think about it on Sunday night, for sure, and then Monday you watch it and kind of get rid of it.

"This time it was Thursday, and Friday, and Saturday, and we got in there on Sunday. It just felt longer."

Drake Maye Knows Patriots Must Correct Costly Mistakes

Maye had plenty to consider during the extended break.

The Patriots held a 10-0 lead late in the third quarter but could not close out the Seahawks. Maye threw three interceptions in the fourth quarter, including one in the end zone with 26 seconds remaining that eliminated New England's final opportunity to win.

Head coach Mike Vrabel said after the game that the Patriots wanted Maye to remain aggressive without becoming reckless. The young quarterback delivered a similar assessment after having several days to review his performance.

New England cannot afford to let one loss follow it into the next week. However, Maye also knows that moving on does not mean ignoring the problems that led to the defeat.

"At the same time, it's something this league is about," Maye said. "It's about playing a game you wish you could have done things better and being able to bounce back."

The Patriots have only played one game, but Maye understands how quickly a season can move. New England will have to eliminate the turnovers and late-game breakdowns before facing the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sept. 20.

"You realize it's Week 1, but at the same time, you have to fix these things quick and in a hurry," Maye said. "Because these things are not going to win you football games. It's the stuff that gets you beat."

The extra time gave Maye an opportunity to confront every costly mistake. Now the Patriots need to prove they learned from them.

articles.title: Michael Porter Jr. Has a Julius Randle Theory That Leads Him to One Very Bold Nets Prediction
articles.summary: Michael Porter Jr. averaged 24.2 points, 7.1 rebounds and 3.0 assists in his first season with the Brooklyn Nets after being traded from Denver last summer,...
articles.body:
Michael Porter Jr . averaged 24.2 points, 7.1 rebounds and 3.0 assists in his first season with the Brooklyn Nets after being traded from Denver last summer, though a hamstring injury limited him to 52 games and ended his season early in March. Heading into 2026-27, his final contract year, Porter is making bold predictions about where Brooklyn is headed.

The forward recently claimed that he expects the Nets to win 50 games this season, a target that sits well above any outside projection for a team that finished well below .500 last year.

Michael Porter Jr. sees Julius Randle as Brooklyn's path to 50 wins

Porter believes teammate Julius Randle's ability to attack the basket can create easier shots for the Nets. Randle can force defenders to help, then pass out to Porter for open three-pointers. Porter explained the pairing in a recent interview shared by The Dunk Central.

"Like, because he can draw a double team. He can get downhill, draw a double team, and then like swing it to me. I can shoot three." Porter described the role of Randle and his own shooting in the interview.

Porter then connected that fit to Brooklyn's young players. He also added, "Like, yeah, I think if we get that chemistry right, all of our young guys from last year got so much better, bro. Like, I don't know what the expectations are for our team, but we're going to definitely surpass them. So you think y'all are passing the 50 win mark? Yeah, I do."

The prediction is far higher than the expectations around the Nets. Brooklyn has spent recent seasons developing its young core, and Porter now sees enough progress to believe the group can compete for 50 wins. Randle's playmaking and Porter's shooting give the offense two clear strengths, but the rest of the roster must turn that idea into steady production.

Brooklyn's young core faces an early reality check

The Nets will have to prove the prediction in regular-season games. Recent league projections show how much distance sits between bold team optimism and outside expectations.

Brooklyn cannot depend on Randle and Porter to solve every problem. The young players must defend, move the ball, and stay consistent across a long schedule.

The first weeks will provide the clearest answer. If the Nets defend well and Randle's passing creates the openings Porter expects, the 50-win target may become a serious goal. If not, the prediction will remain an offseason promise. The Nets will need the same kind of team growth seen across other rebuilding NBA groups.

articles.title: 2X NBA Champion Says Giannis-Bam Adebayo Frontcourt Is Living Cheat Code for Heat Offense
articles.summary: Bam Adebayo has spent years carrying a heavy load for the Miami Heat without needing much help to define his game. He has defended the other team’s best bigs...
articles.body:
Bam Adebayo has spent years carrying a heavy load for the Miami Heat without needing much help to define his game. He has defended the other team's best bigs, created from the middle of the floor and taken on whatever offensive job the matchup demanded.

That could look different next season. Mario Chalmers believes the arrival of Giannis Antetokounmpo could give Adebayo a new lane on offense without taking away the role that has made him so valuable on defense.

Bam Adebayo Could Show More Of His Offensive Game

Chalmers sees room for Adebayo to stretch the floor more, particularly from three-point range. The idea is not to turn him into a different player, but to give him more chances to use skills that have often taken a back seat to everything else Miami asks from him.

"I think Bam is going to show his versatility more, his 3PT shot more. I expect more from Bam this year but still the defensive anchor and that guy he's always been," Chalmers said .

That last part matters. Bam Adebayo does not need to stop being the Heat's defensive anchor for his offense to grow, and Chalmers clearly does not expect that tradeoff.

The bigger change could come from where Adebayo gets his chances. With another elite player handling a large share of the defensive attention, Bam may not have to manufacture every scoring opportunity himself.

That is where Chalmers' prediction gets more interesting. Antetokounmpo can put a defense in a bind the moment he gets downhill, and those possessions can create the kind of clean perimeter looks that are harder to find when Adebayo carries more of the creation burden.

"I'm expecting Bam to have more open looks than he's ever had in his career playing alongside Giannis," Chalmers said.

For Bam Adebayo, those chances could come without a major change to his responsibilities. He can still screen, attack mismatches and anchor the defense, then step outside when Giannis draws help.

The Heat have already leaned on Adebayo as one of their most trusted players. Chalmers is betting that Giannis can make the next part of his game easier to see.

That would give Bam a different kind of offensive lane in Miami, one built less on creating everything himself and more on exploiting the attention his new teammate commands.

articles.body:
Baker Mayfield's confidence in his alma mater backfired Saturday when his Oklahoma Sooners suffered an upset loss to Michigan and left him on the losing end of a bet with his head coach.

articles.title: Bayern Munich announces contract extension for sporting director Christoph Freund
articles.summary: FC Bayern is getting some work done.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich has made another important commitment to the club's sporting structure, announcing that sporting director Christoph Freund has signed a contract extension through June 30, 2029 per the club website .

Freund, 49, joined Bayern Munich in the summer of 2023 after spending 17 years in management at RB Salzburg. Since arriving in Munich, he has been part of a period that has already produced two Bundesliga titles, a DFB-Pokal, and two Franz Beckenbauer Supercups.

Bayern Munich CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen emphasized just how important Freund has become to the club's sporting operation.

"Christoph Freund plays a central role in all of our sporting decisions – and we are pleased that he will continue to work for FC Bayern in the future. The successes of recent years are in part thanks to his stellar work. Christoph maintains an excellent working relationship with Vincent Kompany, is closely involved with the team and, at the same time, keeps a close eye on all sporting matters," Dreesen said. "When he joined FC Bayern in 2023, we expected him not only to provide important impetus for our first team, but also to bring a fresh approach to youth development and the link between the first team and the Campus. He has more than fulfilled those expectations, and we look forward to continuing to develop our whole sporting division together with him."

Board member for sport Max Eberl also highlighted Freund's importance across the club.

"I am delighted that Christoph will continue to work with all of us on FC Bayern's sporting direction. Christoph is a valuable member of our team and a central figure in the sporting division, from the first team and staff down to the FC Bayern Campus. We complement each other in our day-to-day work, enjoy working together and are always guided by the shared goal of constantly pushing FC Bayern forward," Eberl stated.

With Freund now tied down through 2029 and Eberl also recently inking a contract extension, Bayern Munich has secured continuity in a key part of the sporting leadership structure.

articles.title: Edgardo Henriquez Gets Positive MRI, Dodgers Hopeful for Postseason Return
articles.summary: Dodgers key reliever Edgardo Henriquez got the official diagnosis for his lower-body injury that has him on the injured list.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers key reliever Edgardo Henriquez got the official diagnosis for his lower-body injury that has him on the injured list.

Henriquez has a "low-grade" back strain, and the team is "hopeful" he'll be back for the postseason, manager Dave Roberts said.

Roberts described the MRI results as "positive," which should be a relief for fans hoping to get their best bullpen arm back in time for the playoffs.

The Dodgers placed him on the 15-day injured list, meaning that he is not eligible to return until September 29th, effectively ending his regular season.

All eyes will be on Henriquez as we look toward October, when he is expected to be a high-leverage arm, possibly even the closer if he is able to get back to pitching again soon.

Why Henriquez is so important for the Dodgers

Henriquez has a 2.62 ERA, with a 2.50 FIP. He misses the barrel of the bat, strikes out hitters, and limits home runs like one of the best relievers.

He throws triple digits, which may explain his back issue, but the pitch's movement and growing command make it a deadly weapon out of the bullpen.

While he lacks the high-leverage experience of players like Edwin Diaz and Tanner Scott , Henriquez carries himself confidently and exudes a strong presence whenever he takes the mound.

It is unclear how quickly the Dodgers will pull the trigger on Henriquez in the playoffs for a high-leverage role, but given what he has proven this year, they will try to lean on him as much as his health permits.

articles.title: Vic Fangio on Jalen Carter’s conditioning Week 1: “It wasn’t terrible”
articles.summary: The Eagles DC explained why he was disappointed after Week 1, and why Moro Ojomo’s stop was so impressive.
articles.body:
The Eagles are now moving on from their season opener, but DC Vic Fangio spoke on Tuesday about some of the issues the defense faced against the Commanders, on why Moro Ojomo 's stop was so impressive, and what he expects from Cam Ward and the Titans in Week 2.

Fangio was asked about his overall takeaway from the Week 1 win, and he didn't hold back.

"Disappointed in their three scoring drives. There's some scoring drives you give up where the other team just beats you. They've got good players and good coaches, too. But I think we could have played a little better in some of those instances from our just overall play, so that was a little frustrating."

"The last two drives there, we just didn't play well enough. The quarterback scrambling hurt us some. It wasn't good the last couple for sure."

Fangio was asked about Cooper DeJean 's post-game comments about his eyes get bad and that's what hurts him. The DC agreed that can happen at times, but also noted at other times, that quality has helped him.

"[Cooper DeJean]'s just got to make sure he can stay tight enough to his assignment and not let his vision get too skewed to where he gets out of position."

The DC also gave all the credit to Ojomo for sniffing out the play because it wasn't something the Commanders had put on film prior to the game.

"It was just a great play by him individually. Like he said, he saw the guard pull, so he immediately tried to cross the guy that was trying to block him, which he did successfully and made the play. Was a big play by him obviously, but to have the energy and the wherewithal to do that that late in the game was big."

Fangio later talked about about Ojomo's play and how his instincts are both natural and something he works on. He also highlighted the effort Ojomo plays with and how that impacts things as well.

"But [Ojomo] does have good instincts, but he gives great effort and he's tenacious."

" It wasn't terrible. We did have a lot of reps, but a good bit of them came the last drive of the first half and then those last two drives. Those other drives were kind of shorter in duration, so it's a little easier to play that many."

Fangio was very complimentary of Titans QB Cam Ward, noting that the quarterback has very good arm talent, and he's athletic and mobile. The DC said Ward is progressing well and thinks the QB will continue to improve in Tennessee 's offense.

He also said that new Titans OC Brian Daboll does a good job of calling the game and has a good run-pass mix. Fangio expects Tennessee to take some shots in the passing game, but also get a mix of some quicker throws.

"I think [Brian Daboll] does a good job of mixing it up, not just run and pass, but the types of run and passes, too."

Fangio said that Jihaad Campbell "did fine" in the season opener, but said that there were plays he'd like back.

The DC revealed that OLB AJ Epenesa got dinged up in the game against the Commanders, which is why OLB Arnold Ebiketie got more reps.

He said that second-year safety Andrew Mukuba did a good job communicating on the backend, although Fangio added that the performance wasn't perfect, but it was good.

Fangio also said that the safety duo of Mukuba and Marcus Epps did fine, even though he noted that there were some plays that could have gone better from an assignment or execution standpoint.

The DC said he's very pleased with CB Riq Woolen 's performance, and thought he had good focus and did a good job covering.

He also explained that Zack Baun was able to participate in all of training camp, unlike last year, and Fangio highlighted that more practice tends to lead to better game performances. Still, the DC said he appreciates everything from what Baun was able to do on Sunday, and the LB played really well.
